To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the TP53 gene mutations in the Li-Fraumenis Syndrome (LFS) are associated with different tumors.
the R337P mutation in the TP53 gene is associated with a high risk of developing adrenocortica carcinoma and acute lymphoblastic leukaemia in children.

the R337P mutation is associated with a high risk of ACC in children, and the presence of this mutation in a child with ACC should prompt the search for the TP53 mutation in other members of the family, including asymptomatic relatives, in order to identify carriers.
